extracted.intended_audience: IP office statisticians, policymakers, researchers, and practitioners in intellectual property (trademarks)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and methodological notes used in WIPO's trademark statistical tables and figures (selection thresholds, definitions, calculation rules, data-coverage caveats) for preparing and interpreting trademark statistics in the World Intellectual Property Indicators report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for selected 20 origins (2023, GDP & class count)
rubrics_metrics.description: The selected 20 origins for 2023 were included if they had a GDP greater than USD 250 billion PPP and a resident trademark application class count of at least 20,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This figure does not provide an overall ranking of all origins; rather, it shows a selection across geographical regions and income groups. Sources: WIPO Statistics Database and World Bank, August 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for selected 20 origins (2013/2023, population & class count)
rubrics_metrics.description: The selected 20 origins for 2023 were included if they had a population greater than 2.8 million and a resident trademark application class count of at least 2,600.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This figure does not provide an overall ranking of all origins; rather, it shows a selection across geographical regions and income groups. Sources: WIPO Statistics Database and World Bank, August 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: trademark registrations in force
rubrics_metrics.description: Data refer to the number of trademark registrations in force, not the number of classes specified in those registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trademark rights can be maintained indefinitely by paying a renewal fee at defined intervals. 'Trademarks in force' provides information on the volume of trademark registrations currently active, as well as the historical trademark life cycle. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of registration-year percentages (registrations in force by registration year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentages are calculated as follows: the number of trademark registrations issued in year t and in force in 2023 divided by the total number of trademark registrations issued in year t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This figure is based on about 24.3 million active trademark registrations reported by the 88 offices that provided a breakdown by year of registration. Detailed data for several of the larger offices, such as those of China and Japan, are unavailable. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonization caveat when comparing offices
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO collects data from IP offices using a common questionnaire and methodology; however, due to differences in the application processing procedures between offices, data cannot be fully harmonized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore, caution should be exercised when making comparisons across offices. This caveat is repeated for multiple figures (examination outcomes, pending applications, examiners, durations, etc.). Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote-based data completeness and special-case rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple footnotes indicate when data are incomplete or represent special cases (e.g., (a) data by origin incomplete because some offices do not report detailed statistics; (b) only Madrid designation data available; (c) country without national office; (d) resident applications include filings from multiple territories; (e) resident includes EU member states; (f) aggregate direct counts cannot be broken down; (g) OAPI is competent office; (h) non‑Madrid member jurisdictions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users must consult and apply these footnotes when interpreting application/registration class counts by office and origin; missing or aggregated reporting alters comparability. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination outcome categories and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of trademark examination outcomes is reported by category: Registered, Total rejection, Withdrawn/abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because offices have different application processing procedures and reporting conventions, outcome shares reported by WIPO should be interpreted with caution and understood as coming from office-supplied questionnaires. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending applications and office-level pending counts
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO reports 'Potentially pending trademark applications' for selected offices as counts supplied by offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These counts are compiled from office responses; due to differing procedures and definitions across offices, cross-office comparisons require caution. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration metrics for trademark examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration of trademark examination is reported for selected offices in average days, separately for 'First office action' and 'Final decision'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are office-supplied averages; differences in procedural practices across offices mean durations are not fully harmonized and comparisons should be made cautiously. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of collective and certification trademark application counts (top offices)
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO reports counts of collective trademark applications and certification trademark applications for the top 20 offices (by count) in 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes clarify office identities (e.g., EUIPO is European Union Intellectual Property Office; BOIP is Benelux Office for Intellectual Property). The ranking reflects reported counts and the selection of 'top 20' for the figure, not an exhaustive global ranking. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2024.
